In particular, Eq. ( 11 ) suggests that a practitioner should apply LoRA finetuning to layers whose corresponding NTK have large minimum eigenvalue, driving the spectrum of F F to 0 0 . This finding is consistent with Theorem 7 of Afzal et al. () in a generic fine-tuning setup (not LoRA), where the authors also advocate selecting layers that increase the minimum eigenvalue of the NTK to reduce the empirical risk. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first to connect the NTK spectrum to LoRA expressivity to this level of precision. sections.heading: 5 The CG-LoRA algorithm
6 Experiments
sections.text: We perform a preliminary evaluation of the performance of CG-LoRA on standard natural language understanding tasks. To ensure a fair comparison, all algorithms are run under identical conditions, controlling for sources of variability such as random seeds, learning rates, and input tokenization. As a result, the performance of baseline methods may differ from that reported in prior work, since we do not rely on their original implementations. Our experiments were conducted using an NVIDIA A40 GPU. All our results are fully reproducible and will be made available in a final version. 6.1 Implementation details Baselines. Our results are compared against full finetuning and several variants of LoRA, namely 1) LoRA-GA, 2) LoRA-One, 3) rsLoRA. We decide to focus on these particular variants which are the most related, current state-of-the-art. We used the available implementation of LoRA-GA, which can directly be attached to any LoRA model from Hugging Face. For LoRA-One, we re-implemented their exact algorithm by reusing loss gradients computed by LoRA-GA. We also reused their global scaling parameters provided in their Appendix G.4. Models and common LoRA parameters. We consider finetuning T5-base and RoBERTa-base models with various LoRA methods applied to the same linear layers. We fix the LoRA rank r = 8 r=8 and consider the rsLoRA scaling for all methods η = 2 ​ r \eta={2\sqrt{r}} . To keep the computational overhead low, all non-zero based initialization methods CG-LoRA, LoRA-GA, LoRA-One are run with B init = 16 B_{\mathrm{init}}=16 and we accumulate them 32 times yielding an effective dataset of size N = 512 N=512 . Datasets and metrics. We consider several GLUE datasets and evaluate accuracy on a separate test dataset. For a text to text architecture such as T5-base, the input sentences are further preprocessed to be task-specific ("classify the grammaticality of {sentence}" for CoLA). We report standard multiclass accuracy values using predicted probabilities. For T5-base, we compute the true multi-token class probability while LoRA-GA considers only the first token class probability. CG-LoRA hyperparameters. Our proposed algorithm requires three hyperparameters: 1) the oversampling factor m m for the sketching matrix, 2) the number of power iterations q q . 3) the scaling factor γ \gamma . To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we consider low values m = r , q = 1 m=r,q=1 . We also choose γ = 16 \gamma=16 , as considered in Wang et al. (2024) . Shifted initialization. We investigate empirically the effect of starting from the same pre-trained model W 0 W_{0} , denoted by CG-LoRA (shift), versus starting from the shifted initialization W 0 + η ​ B 0 ​ A 0 W_{0}+\eta B_{0}A_{0} , denoted by CG-LoRA (no shift). Training. We use the standard Hugging Face optimizer with AdamW for all methods. We use a cosine learning rate scheduler and find the learning rate by grid search. Candidate values are chosen from { 2 ​ e − 5 , 5 ​ e − 5 , 1 ​ e − 4 , 2 ​ e − 4 , 5 ​ e − 4 , 8 ​ e − 4 } \{2e-5,5e-5,1e-4,2e-4,5e-4,8e-4\} , and they are compared using a separate validation dataset. We fix the training batch size to B train = 32 B_{\mathrm{train}}=32 samples and perform a single full pass on the training dataset. The evaluation batch size is fixed at B eval = 64 B_{\mathrm{eval}}=64 . We run finetuning using three different seeds and report average values as well as standard deviations. 6.2 Results on RoBERTa Table 1: Evaluation accuracy of finetuned RoBERTa-base on GLUE datasets MNLI SST-2 CoLA QNLI MRPC Full 86.89 ± 0.24 \pm 0.24 93.42 ± 0.14 \pm 0.14 80.24 ± 1.22 \pm 1.22 92.04 ± 0.08 \pm 0.08 79.57 ± 5.20 \pm 5.20 rsLoRA 85.54 ± 0.18 \pm 0.18 92.96 ± 0.48 \pm 0.48 79.16 ± 0.16 \pm 0.16 77.25 ± 19.65 \pm 19.65 78.34 ± 1.33 78.34\pm 1.33 LoRA-GA 83.02 ± 0.32 \pm 0.32 93.08 ± 0.19 93.08\pm 0.19 75.03 ± 4.18 \pm 4.18 87.86 ± 0.02 \pm 0.02 76.22 ± 3.81 \pm 3.81 LoRA-One 85.03 ± 0.03 \pm 0.03 92.92 ± 0.28 92.92\pm 0.28 79.02 ± 1.08 \pm 1.08 90.79 ± 0.86 \pm 0.86 76.71 ± 6.05 \pm 6.05 CG-LoRA (no shift) 85.51 ± 0.13 \pm 0.13 93.19 ± 0.14 \pm 0.14 80.53 ± 0.43 \pm 0.43 91.43 ± 0.18 \pm 0.18 82.27 ± 2.71 \pm 2.71 CG-LoRA (shift) 85.35 ± 0.03 \pm 0.03 93.19 ± 0.10 \pm 0.10 72.77 ± 5.15 \pm 5.15 91.14 ± 0.13 \pm 0.13 75.40 ± 4.69 \pm 4.69 On all tested datasets, CG-LoRA has better accuracy than LoRA-GA and LoRA-One as presented by Table 1 . This can be explained by the fact that at the start of finetuning, the gradients are noisy due to the random weights of the head classifier. Since both LoRA-GA and LoRA-One directly initialize their adapters w.r.t the singular value decomposition of the loss gradients, their proposed A 0 , B 0 A_{0},B_{0} can suffer from such noise. On the other hand, the whitened gradient essentially cancels out the noise through renormalization of the loss gradients as discussed in Section 4. Consequently, our proposed initialization is more informative and allows for a faster decrease of the training loss, see Figure 2 , especially for small datasets such as CoLA and MRPC. Noisy pretrained gradients also explain that the non-shifted version outperforms the shifted version which starts at noisy W 0 + η ​ B 0 ​ A 0 W_{0}+\eta B_{0}A_{0} . Figure 2: Performance of finetuned RoBERTa-base on CoLA. The robustness of our initialization to random effects is also supported by Figure 3 , which shows that CG-LoRA (no shift) is less sensitive to a wider array of learning rates, as well as noticeably smaller standard deviation across runs. Figure 3: Evaluation accuracy of finetuned RoBERTa-base on CoLA w.r.t learning rate 6.3 Results on T5-base In this setting, the results obtained are more balanced. Since T5-base is a text to text architecture, the pretrained gradients are naturally informative for the finetuning task, and CG-LoRA performs as well as previous state-of-the art initialization methods. The cost of each operation is calculated for all LoRA layers (24 layers for RoBERTa-base), and is compared to a single batched forward pass which has unit cost 1 1 . In total, we perform 2 ​ q + 1 2q+1 backward passes where q q is the number of power iterations chosen for the Rayleigh Ritz method. The factor 2 2 comes from computing ( Y S , Y T ) (Y_{S},Y_{T}) and ( B S , B T ) (B_{S},B_{T}) . The additional + 1 +1 represents the backward pass required to compute the loss gradient.
